subject.title: Session→model/runtime binding drift persists across doctor --fix --deep because the repair's provider-ownership registry is missing the literal id "openai"

question: Should canonical `openai` session route state be owned for doctor cleanup by the Codex app-server contract, a new OpenAI provider doctor contract, or a generic provider-state repair path?
rationale: Literal `openai` is both the canonical OpenAI provider and the default Codex app-server route in current OpenClaw; source shows adding it to Codex ownership would likely fix the report, but that may conflate canonical OpenAI API state with Codex-owned legacy aliases.

options.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
options.body: Add an `extensions/openai/doctor-contract-api.ts` owner for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and focused tests for auto fallback cleanup, leaving Codex to legacy aliases and Codex runtime ids.

options.title: Codex owns the app-server OpenAI route
options.body: Add `openai` to the Codex doctor owner if maintainers consider OpenAI model-agent runs primarily owned by the Codex app-server route.

options.title: Make the repair generic
options.body: Move stale auto fallback cleanup into provider-agnostic doctor logic whenever the configured route no longer includes the override provider.

recommendation.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
recommendation.body: Add an `extensions/openai/doctor-contract-api.ts` owner for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and focused tests for auto fallback cleanup, leaving Codex to legacy aliases and Codex runtime ids.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior merged doctor/Codex route-state repair PRs make this the clearest available owner-boundary decision signal.
